summaries.gardner: BMO is a 209-year-old Canadian bank in a mature industry, the opposite of the young, fast-growing top dog Gardner looks for. Its shares have momentum (up about 27% over the past year on the NYSE as BMO), but it lacks a breakthrough product, a visionary founder or an emerging-industry lead.
summaries.buffett: BMO has the understandable, regulated franchise Buffett likes in banks, with sticky deposits in Canada's Big Five oligopoly and dividends paid every year since 1829. Against that, its reported ROE was only 10.6% in FY2025, the US expansion via Bank of the West has earned weak returns, and at about 18.6x trailing earnings and roughly 2.1x book value there is little margin of safety.
summaries.munger: Munger would see a durable but ordinary bank: an oligopoly position in Canada and a long record, but leverage of about 17x equity and a costly US acquisition that management is now partly unwinding. It is a fair business at a full price rather than a great business at a fair price.
summaries.lynch: BMO fits Lynch's stalwart category, with FY2025 revenue up 10.6% to C$36,274M and consensus adjusted EPS growth of about 21% in FY2026 as US returns recover. The story is simple (fix US profitability, buy back shares, keep raising the dividend), but at about 16x forward earnings it is not a bargain for a stalwart.
summaries.fisher: Fisher would find a competent, well-capitalised bank (CET1 13.0%) investing in digital and AI tools such as BMO Insurance's Smart Decision underwriting and the Lumi assistant. But it has no standout research-driven product pipeline, and its sales growth is tied to the economy, so it only partly fits his growth-company points.
summaries.graham: BMO passes Graham's tests on size, a dividend paid every year since 1829 and steady profitability in each of the last six fiscal years. It fails his valuation tests: about 18.6x trailing and about 27x three-year-average earnings, with P/E times P/B of about 39, well above 22.5.
summaries.thiel: BMO has no proprietary technology or monopoly built from a small niche; it is one of five big Canadian banks and a mid-sized US bank selling similar products. Its main durable advantage is regulated scale, so it fits Thiel's 'zero to one' questions poorly.
summaries.gerstner: Gerstner looks for durable compounders riding big platform shifts at sensible prices with disciplined costs. BMO is cutting costs and selling non-core businesses to lift ROE toward 15% by fiscal 2027, but it is not a leading beneficiary of AI or cloud and its growth is modest.
summaries.druckenmiller: Druckenmiller focuses on earnings momentum and liquidity: BMO's adjusted EPS rose 22% year on year in Q3 2026 and the stock is up about 27% in a year. But the outlook depends on interest rates, credit and the Canadian economy amid tariffs, and the price already reflects much of the recovery.
summaries.smith: Terry Smith wants high returns on capital without much debt, which banks cannot offer: BMO's reported ROE was 10.6% in FY2025 on heavy leverage. Its business is steady but it does not meet the 'good company' test of his approach.
summaries.greenblatt: Greenblatt's Magic Formula excludes banks because return on capital and earnings yield are not meaningful for them. On a simple earnings basis, a P/E of about 18.6 gives an earnings yield of about 5.4%, not cheap enough to stand out.
summaries.akre: Akre's three-legged stool needs a great business, talented and honest managers, and great reinvestment opportunities. BMO has honest, competent management and a durable franchise, but its returns on equity (10.6% reported in FY2025) and reinvestment opportunities are ordinary.
summaries.pabrai: Pabrai looks for simple businesses in temporary distress at deep discounts with low downside. BMO is simple and its downside is limited by regulation and capital (CET1 13.0%), but after a 27% one-year rise and with the stock near analysts' average target it is not a distressed bargain.
summaries.wood: BMO is a traditional bank, not a disruptive-innovation platform company of the kind ARK targets. Its AI use is internal efficiency, and it is more likely to be disrupted by fintech than to lead it.
summaries.ackman: Ackman favours simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative businesses with dominant positions and strong balance sheets. BMO is simple and has a moat in Canada, but it is a highly leveraged bank whose earnings swing with credit and rates, and it is not dominant in the US.
summaries.sleep: Nick Sleep looked for scale-economics-shared companies whose position strengthens over time. BMO does not pass scale savings back to customers in a way that makes it ever harder to compete with, and its position in 10-20 years is not clearly stronger than today.
summaries.valentine: Valentine sought huge, fast-growing markets and technology-driven start-ups. A 1817-founded bank in a mature market is far outside that approach.
summaries.nash: BMO passes some of Nash's screens on scale, profitability and a 0.84% short interest, but fails hard ones: revenue growth is below 10% (8.7% in nine-month FY2026), bank leverage fails the banker's-lending test and free cash flow is not meaningful. It scores about 60 of 130 on his 13 categories.

momentum.evidence: BMO's NYSE shares rose about 27% over the 52 weeks to mid-October 2026, closing at US$167.07 on October 16, 2026 against a 52-week range of US$119.84 to US$187.22.

g4.evidence: CEO Darryl White has run BMO since 2017 and institutions hold about 51% of the NYSE-listed float, but there are no famous, influential backers beyond ordinary index and bank investors.

g6.evidence: Analysts mostly rate it Hold (15 analysts) with an average target of about US$165.74, close to the price, rather than calling it wildly overvalued.

simple.evidence: BMO is a traditional bank earning C$21,487M of net interest income and C$14,787M of non-interest revenue in FY2025, a model a careful generalist can follow.

b2.evidence: BMO has been profitable every year from FY2020 to FY2025, but net income swung from C$13,537M in FY2022 to C$4,437M in FY2023 before recovering to C$8,725M in FY2025.

integrity.evidence: BMO has been on Ethisphere's World's Most Ethical Companies list nine years in a row (2026) and reports clearly, but the US$16.3 billion Bank of the West purchase has earned weak returns (U.S. Banking ROE 9.8% in Q3 2026).

b6.evidence: The Bank of the West deal was an empire-building move to gain US scale, though management is now selling 138 branches and the Transportation and Vendor Finance businesses to focus capital.

roic.evidence: Reported ROE was 10.6% in FY2025 and 9.7% in FY2024, earned on bank leverage of about 17x equity (C$1,452,112M of liabilities vs C$86,573M of equity at July 31, 2026).

fcf.evidence: Free cash flow is not meaningful for a bank, whose operating cash flow swings with deposit and loan flows.

b10.evidence: Retained earnings funded the Bank of the West purchase and growth, and the share price rose from C$134.37 (Oct 2021) to C$174.23 (Oct 2025), but diluted shares rose from 642.1M in FY2020 to 723.3M in FY2025 and the US deal has returned less than its cost of capital.

safety.evidence: At about C$238 (US$167.07) the stock trades at roughly 2.1x book value of C$113.06 and 18.6x trailing earnings, near analysts' average target, offering little margin of safety.

fairprice.evidence: About 16x consensus FY2026 adjusted EPS of C$14.73 with a 2.9% dividend yield is reasonable for a bank expecting about 21% EPS growth this year, but not cheap for a mature lender.

mu5.evidence: Strong regulation and a 13.0% CET1 ratio limit failure risk, but like any bank it could be badly hurt by a severe credit downturn, a Canadian housing bust or a funding crisis.

reinvest.evidence: Returns on reinvested capital are ordinary (adjusted ROE 14.0% in Q3 2026, U.S. Banking 9.8%), and excess capital is returned via a new buyback of up to 25 million shares.

ly2.evidence: BMO is a clear stalwart with a simple story: lift US returns, cut costs and reach a sustainable 15% ROE exiting fiscal 2027.

ly3.evidence: Forward P/E of about 15-16 is below the roughly 21% FY2026 consensus adjusted EPS growth, but that growth is a one-off recovery and long-run growth is in the high single digits.

runway.evidence: BMO can keep growing with the Canadian and US economies (FY2026 consensus revenue growth about 8%), but it is shrinking parts of its US footprint rather than entering big new markets.

ly7.evidence: BMO repurchased 3.8 million shares in Q3 2026 and plans a buyback of up to 25 million, cutting shares outstanding to 697.1 million, but there is no evidence of notable insider buying.

ly8.evidence: BMO is widely covered by Canadian and US analysts and is a core holding of Canadian dividend investors.

fi2.evidence: BMO keeps launching products such as new ETFs, BMO Blue Rewards and AI-driven insurance underwriting, but these are incremental banking products.

fi3.evidence: BMO does not report R&D spending; its technology investments are part of non-interest expense (C$21,107M in FY2025).

fi4.evidence: BMO shows good sales momentum (premium account growth of 47% and Canadian commercial new-client acquisition up 20% year to date in 2026), but it is not clearly better at selling than RBC or TD.

longterm.evidence: BMO made a long-term bet on the US with Bank of the West and invests in digital, but it is now focused on near-term ROE targets and divestitures.

gr1.evidence: BMO had C$1,538,685M of assets at July 31, 2026 and a market value of about US$116 billion.

ni10.evidence: BMO reported a profit in every fiscal year checked from FY2020 to FY2025, the lowest being C$4,437M in FY2023, and has paid dividends without interruption since 1829.

gr4.evidence: BMO has the longest-running dividend payout record of any company in Canada (since 1829) and declared C$6.44 per share in FY2025.

eps10.evidence: Reported diluted EPS rose from C$7.55 in FY2020 to C$11.44 in FY2025 (+52%) alone, more than one third (FY2015 EPS not checked).

gr6.evidence: At about C$238 the shares trade at about 27x the three-year average diluted EPS of C$8.90 (FY2023-FY2025), well above Graham's 15.

gr7.evidence: A trailing P/E of about 18.6 times P/B of about 2.1 gives about 39, well above Graham's 22.5 ceiling.

th1.evidence: BMO has no proprietary technology ten times better than rivals; its banking products are similar to other big banks'.

timing.evidence: A steeper yield curve and improving credit (PCL fell to C$722M in Q3 2026 from C$797M) help, but tariffs and rate cuts weigh on the Canadian economy.

th3.evidence: BMO did not start by dominating a small niche; it is a broad bank founded in 1817.

team.evidence: Darryl White's team is experienced and steady but not seen as world-class; BMO's reported ROE (10.6% in FY2025) trails the best Canadian peers.

th5.evidence: BMO reaches about 13 million clients through branches, digital channels and commercial relationship managers in Canada and the US.

durable.evidence: Its Canadian Big Five position should hold for decades given regulation, but its US franchise and fee businesses face pressure from larger US banks and fintechs.

th7.evidence: BMO's strategy follows the same North American banking playbook as its peers rather than a unique, unseen opportunity.

trend.evidence: BMO uses AI internally (Lumi assistant, Smart Decision underwriting) but is not a leading beneficiary of a major platform shift.

dr1.evidence: Adjusted EPS rose 22% year on year to C$3.96 in Q3 2026 and consensus expects about 21% adjusted EPS growth for FY2026.

dr2.evidence: Closing the branch, Transportation Finance and Vendor Finance sales should add about 50 bp to CET1 and lift ROE, but the 15% ROE goal is already public and partly priced in.

dr4.evidence: A steeper yield curve and stable credit help, but Bank of Canada rate cuts and tariff pressure on the Canadian economy work against it.

dr6.evidence: Closing the Stonepeak sale of Transportation and Vendor Finance, the new buyback of up to 25 million shares and the Q4 FY2026 results on December 2, 2026 could drive results and the share price.

gm.evidence: Banks do not report a gross margin; BMO's FY2025 pre-tax margin was about 31.8%.

fcfyield.evidence: Free-cash-flow yield is not meaningful for a bank; its dividend yield is about 2.9% and buyback yield about 2.6%.

gb2.evidence: Enterprise value is not meaningful for a bank because deposits and wholesale funding are operating liabilities.

pa2.evidence: BMO's weak US returns after the Bank of the West deal are a fixable setback that management is addressing through branch and business sales, and adjusted ROE has already recovered to 14.0%.

pa4.evidence: A 13.0% CET1 ratio, regulated Canadian franchise and dividends paid since 1829 make permanent loss unlikely, barring a severe financial crisis.

wo1.evidence: BMO is not a leader in AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or multiomic sequencing.

wo3.evidence: BMO does not combine several innovation platforms.

wo4.evidence: Its banking market grows roughly with the economy and will not be many times larger in five years.

ac3.evidence: BMO's earnings depend heavily on interest rates (net interest income was C$21,487M of C$36,274M FY2025 revenue) and on the credit cycle.

ns1.evidence: BMO does not pass scale savings to customers in a way that makes it ever harder to compete with.

ns4.evidence: If it reaches its 15% ROE goal BMO will be more profitable, but its competitive position in 10-20 years is not clearly stronger than today.

va2.evidence: Safe deposits, credit and payments are important needs, but they are already served by many banks.

tn1.evidence: BMO is a traditional bank retrofitting AI tools, not a company built for a secular trend.

tn2.evidence: The market sees BMO as a Canadian and US bank, which is what it is becoming; there is no story gap.

tn3.evidence: BMO is a large-cap North American bank outside Nash's zones to avoid.

tn4.evidence: BMO is profitable (C$8,725M FY2025 net income) and revenue grew in FY2024 and FY2025, but revenue fell in FY2023 and as a bank its liabilities far exceed its cash.

tn5.evidence: Quarterly free cash flow and cash-versus-debt are not meaningful for a bank whose cash flows swing with deposits and trading.

tn9.evidence: BMO trips the revenue-growth kill (8.7% nine-month FY2026 growth, down from 10.6%) and, as a bank, its liabilities far exceed its cash.

tn11.evidence: BMO provides deposits, loans, payments and investment services that help households and businesses in Canada and the US manage and grow money, and charges interest spreads and fees.

tn13.evidence: Total about 60: cash vs debt 5, revenue growth 0, operating margin 10, short interest 10, institutional ownership 5, revenue faster than expenses 10, 5-year return vs S&P 500 0, moat 5, CEO 5, pricing power 5, secular trend 0, culture 0, talent 5.

tn18.evidence: Darryl White has led BMO for nearly nine years with rising profits, but he is not a founder and has not been in the role for 10 years, and there is no record of large open-market purchases.

tn20.evidence: BMO's adjusted EPS of C$3.96 in Q3 2026 was a strong result, but a full record of beats against consensus over the last four quarters was not checked.

tn22.evidence: BMO earns tens of billions in revenue, is profitable and buys back shares rather than issuing them.

tn24.evidence: At about 15-16x forward earnings with a 2.9% yield the price implies mid-to-high single-digit growth, below the current 21% EPS rebound but close to BMO's longer-run growth.
